title: Choose Catch's art direction
question: Round two, in Mr. Morale sepia and Phoenician Scheme colour. Keep one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: The Cutaway
options.lineage: Wes Anderson's cutaway buildings (French Dispatch, Phoenician Scheme sets), shot in Mr. Morale's sepia film
options.thesis: Your archive is a building sliced open like a film set: every catch is a lit room you can look into.
options.viewport: A symmetrical cross-section of a narrow building; each floor is a month, each room a session with its own small scene and brass number; open rooms are lit, closed ones dark; the paste slot is the street-level letterbox.
options.risk: Many sessions means many rooms, so the building must grow floors gracefully and search must stay one tap away.

raised.raise: States are marks, not just colour: a closed room's window gets a drawn blind, never just a dimmer shade.
Nothing vanishes, it closes: read sessions stay in the building, lights off.
A new catch arrives as one event: its room light switches on and the brass number letters in.

options.label: The Film Collection
options.lineage: your cinema idea, reworked as a collector's shelf of numbered box-set spines
options.thesis: Every catch is a film in your private collection, numbered on the spine like a box-set edition.
options.viewport: A shelf of tall spines, each designed differently with its session number; pull one out and its cover and liner notes slide forward.
options.risk: Each link needs its own spine design, so the generator has to stay varied without looking random.

options.label: The Shoebox Archive
options.lineage: the shoeboxes of documents in The Phoenician Scheme
options.thesis: Folders are labelled shoeboxes on a collector's wall; every catch is an index card filed inside.
options.viewport: A symmetrical wall of numbered shoeboxes under a gilt-framed painting; the open box fans its cards forward with session numbers typed on each.
options.risk: Close to the film's own props, so it must not become a fan tribute.

options.label: The Collection Plates
options.thesis: Each catch is a numbered plate in the catalogue of your collection, signed with an attribution stamp.
options.viewport: One large plate for the newest catch with crosshairs at its corners, a rotating attribution stamp half off it, and a hairline credits row below.
options.case: Gives the 'art piece' feeling directly and reads clearly; less warmth and story than the film worlds.
options.risk: Without real artwork per link, plates need a generated image system to avoid empty frames.

options.label: The Stamp Catalogue
options.lineage: convention circle catalogues of hand-drawn thumbnails
options.thesis: Every catch gets a tiny hand-drawn stamp in a numbered grid; open ones are circled in biro.
options.viewport: A dense grid of postage-stamp drawings with codes beneath; open sessions circled by hand, closed ones struck through.
options.case: The most handmade and raw option and easy to scan; less cinematic than your references.
options.risk: The drawings must be generated well or it looks like clip art.

options.label: Concourse Flap Board
options.thesis: Sessions as rows on a clacking board.
options.risk: You already ruled out the departure board.
options.case: Declined: too close to the board you passed on.
options.kept: A new catch arrives as one event, letter by letter.

options.label: Reference Rail
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.case: Declined: a reading page, not a scene.
options.kept: States are marks, not just colours.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.thesis: Folders as coloured lobes of land.
options.risk: Its palette fights the one you asked for.
options.case: Declined: bright and playful where you asked for sepia and oxblood.
options.kept: One shape drives layout, art and state together.
